title: The 11/6 supremum of the Wang-Sitters rounding scheme for graph balancing
summary: Wang and Sitters' 11/6-approximation for graph balancing (each job allowed on at most two machines) is not one algorithm but a set of permitted executions. Step 1 may return any feasible solution of the fractional relaxation. Step 3 may match remaining jobs to the rounding's slots in many ways. We determine exactly what that latitude permits: ratios arbitrarily close to 11/6, none reaching it, so 11/6 is the least constant bounding every permitted run.
